summary: Gate B: PASS (verify OVERALL PASS on every step, Android included). Brief 7.7 stays PENDING_HUMAN. What works: the full game on Windows and Android: menu with the attract match, three biome cards and the color picker; 90 s rounds (1 human + 3 bots); La Revanche with the v1.4 rule (a chased return survives but captures nothing: 'Rentré 0,3 s avant l'étincelle : boucle perdue.', no fill, the thread dissolves); the lasso pocket; results with the WHY line; pause and quit panels; FR/EN strings; procedural sounds per biome; haptics on Android. The three biomes, judged on the probe screenshots at 540x960 (High) and on Medium-tier DevShots (the Android default): LIQUIDE meets V1-V8 of contract 12.5 (glossy puddles with upper-left streaks and lower-right shadows, round threads with concave necks, beads larger than the thread, tapered cut end + droplet chain + teardrop front, exact palette on a grained navy table, no staircase, flat pocket stripes next to raised home). FEU meets 25.3/25.5 (ember beds with live flame edges, burning fuse, fireballs, white-hot spark racing the fuse, embers cooling to ash, flame-front fill, glowing pocket stripes, four distinct flame colors). ÉLECTRICITÉ meets 25.4/25.5 (hex plasma with a neon rim and arcs, live wire, plasma orbs, branching-lightning fill, current packet, dead grey cable, dashed neon pocket, short-circuit burst). No magenta, no broken layering, no exception in any player log. Fixes made by the gate: the tutorial bubble no longer leaves an empty grey box while it fades out (cubic fade), droplets now grow from the cut toward the front as in the reference, the actor-field RT is no longer reallocated on every frame of the chase zoom (size quantized to 32 px), the fire/electric saved return leaves no residual glow, the tutorial pointer reads the spark edge indicator directly (no reflection, safe under IL2CPP stripping), the UI selection is cleared when play starts or resumes, overlay shape ids 6-15 are reserved for biome effects. Tests: dotnet Core 316 passed (318, 2 skipped by design); Unity EditMode 421 run, 0 failures, 2 skipped (419 in the verify run + 2 gate tests added after it); PlayMode 8/8. Verify (docs/verify_last.txt, 14:33): dotnet, setup (ShaderCheck 12 shaders), editmode, playmode, buildwindows (93.8 MB), probe liquid fps30 + fps144 (equal hash 246577239DE179C4), probe fire and probe electric (same hash), android: all PASS. APK: Build/Android/PainterIO.apk, 32.4 MB, VIBRATE present. Windows release: Build/Windows/PainterIO.exe (tools/run.cmd launches it, '-biome fire|electric' optional). Known defects / not verified: nothing was run on an Android device (perf, touch, haptics, safe area, GLES3 fallback); no human has listened to the sounds; the fill re-uploads the whole 1 MB visual mask each fill frame (Android cost unknown); on GLES 3.0 devices the fire fill front may show cell-sized blocks (no Gather); ring, charge ring and edge indicators were only seen in the -actorgallery harness, not in a sim-driven screenshot; time effects (flicker, arcs, burn-out) were judged from single frames.

api_additions: ActorFieldCamera.QuantizeSide(float pixels, int maxSide) (public static int): exact side rounded up to a multiple of RtQuantum, clamped to [16, maxSide]
contract_issues: 12.2 item 2 / 19: the actor RT size is round(R.size * ppu * tierScale) rounded UP to a multiple of 32 px. The exact formula drifted by a few px on most frames of the chase zoom (the 0.6 u margin is in world units while ppu changes), which reallocated the RT every frame of each zoom ease. Consumers map through _PIO_ActorRect and _PIO_ActorTexel, so the slightly denser RT changes nothing visible (B3's need).

12.3 droplets 'visible radius 0.07 to 0.12, deterministic per index': kept, and the radius now grows with the chain index (0.07-0.085 next to the cut, about 0.11 after 9 droplets) as in docs/reference_gouttes.png (LIQ's need). FireFx reads the same RetractionView.DropletRadius, so the fire ember chain follows.

15.4 (no text on fades): the tutorial bubble and its pointer fade out on a cubic curve. A linear fade of the light bubble over the dark fire and electric grounds showed an empty grey slab for about 0.1 s (seen in the saved checkpoint by B6, FIRE and ELEC).
18.4: verify also runs probe-fire and probe-electric (B6 reading, kept). Gate B judged them on the merged tree: same hash 246577239DE179C4 in all biomes.

Readings to fold into the contract by its owner (listed in the wave B reports under contract_issues, not applied to CONTRACT.md by the gate): B3 (camera and input readings, SteeringInput order -200), B4 (UI readings), B5 (sound readings, section 16), B6 (probe shot names, biome probe steps, stricter checks), BI (_PIO_RevealTime on the sim render clock, BiomeTheme.SetCurrent, SecondaryColors / ShaderParams globals), FIRE (bead kind classified by radius, reveal sentinel), ELEC (orb-arc distance, flicker rate, shape ids), LIQ (shadow reach 1.5x, gloss 130 + streak term, fusion flare, union height, vignette and grain).
open_issues: Brief 7.7 is PENDING_HUMAN: docs/playtest_7_7.md is ready (install with 'adb install -r Build/Android/PainterIO.apk', 3 rounds lasso off then 3 lasso on, optional fire and electric rounds). No agent may mark it passed.

Counts: 'passing' 743 = dotnet 316 (318 total, 2 skipped by design) + EditMode 419 (TestResults/gateB_edit_final.xml: 421 run, 0 failures, 2 skipped Core BotReport cases) + PlayMode 8 (TestResults/gateB_play.xml). The full verify (docs/verify_last.txt) ran before the 2 gate tests were added (419 EditMode tests there); the gate tests touch no runtime code, so the verified builds are unchanged.

Verify results (full run 14:33 with -Android -KeepGoing, agent gateB): dotnet PASS (128 s), setup PASS (ShaderCheck 12 shaders, 0 failures), editmode PASS 419/0/2, playmode PASS 8/0, buildwindows PASS (93.8 MB), probe liquid fps30 PASS avgMs 33.40 + fps144 PASS avgMs 7.01 with equal hash 246577239DE179C4, probe-fire PASS (avgMs 16.73 at the 60 fps cap), probe-electric PASS (avgMs 16.74), android PASS (32.4 MB, VIBRATE present, 316 s). A baseline run before the gate fixes was also all PASS. Perf numbers are from the dev PC (Intel iGPU, D3D11, tier High): frames are capped, not slow.

Visual review (docs/waveB/shots/gate): liquid V1-V8 pass; fire 25.3 and electric 25.4 pass; 25.5 readability pass (four distinct colors per biome, home / pocket / rival identifiable, the spark or packet is the brightest moving point; on Medium without bloom the fire spark is less dominant but still the brightest point on the fuse). The first-cut tutorial pointer ring frames the front (by design of 15.4); the danger vignette is a red screen edge while chased.

Not verified on a device (none attached): Android frame time on Medium (FireComposite and ElectricComposite cost more ALU than the liquid one, still within the fetch budget), touch steering, haptics, safe area, Android back, renderScale on screens taller than 1920 px, the GLES3 fallback subshaders.

Fill upload: TerritoryField re-uploads the whole 512x512 RGBA32 visual mask (1 MB) on every frame of a fill or evaporation (about 21 frames per capture at 60 fps, 36 in fire). Fine on PC; the Android cost is unmeasured. A partial upload (staging texture + CopyTexture of the dirty rectangle) is the fix if a device shows stutter during fills.

_PIO_RevealTime keeps the -1000 sentinel for cells present at session start. Shaders without Gather (GLES 3.0 variants) use a bilinear fallback whose fire fill front can show cell-sized blocks; the liquid ripple keeps a faint texel step where new liquid meets old (LIQ). An 'old but finite' sentinel (FIRE's suggestion) would soften both; left as is to stay on contract 25.2.

ShaderCheck compiles only the active subshader of each graph: an error that exists only in the lower-target subshader (FIRE hit GatherRed in ps_4_0) is caught by BuildWindows / BuildAndroid, not by SetupAndCompile. Both builds are part of verify, so it cannot slip through, only later.

Ring, charge ring, ring indicator and spark edge indicator were verified only through the -actorgallery harness (B2); no demo checkpoint shows them driven by sim events. The probe's 20 s bot round runs with lasso on and logs no exception.
Time-based effects (fire burn-out, electric short-circuit flicker and lightning hops, wire jag, exit pop, merge squash) were judged from single frames and the agents' window captures.
Sounds were never heard by a human (B5, FIRE, ELEC verified them numerically). Please audition a round per biome.
B2's rare crash at quit: not reproduced (8 probe runs and 3 DevShot runs by the gate, all exit 0).

Liquid details left as accepted limits: pearl highlight is a few pixels at 30 px/u; thread to pearl width ratio 1:2.6 (contract-fixed radii) against about 1:4 in the reference; a faint shading change can remain where a widened neck covers the bevel (visible only at 3x zoom).
